item.title: Doctor Who: Season 7
item.description:
Another season! There are a number of weak ones in this season, but oh man the highs are high. Especially the finale and transition to Season 8. Oh, I’m looking forward to that!

minor spoilers It’s quite a season for the last we see of the Ponds and Eleven's last run. Not to mention the introduction (several times!) of Clara . Oh, and a multi-doctor story! with Ten, Eleven, and the War Doctor! .

Quite a season.

Onward!

item.title: The House of Hades
item.description:
To say this series keeps escalating is putting it mildly.

What start a tale of demigods has already grown to include the gods, Titans, and giants, but it just keeps getting bigger and bigger.

This time around, we have two plots. In one, five of the seven still battling their way across the Mediterranean and fighting for their lives the whole way. Hazel in particular steps up a lot of this book–which, it’s the Hades one, so it makes sense.

item.title: The Tombs of Atuan
item.description:
Freedom is a heavy load, a great and strange burden for the spirit to undertake. It is not easy. It is not a gift given, but a choice made, and the choice may be a hard one. The road goes upward towards the light; but the laden traveler may never reach the end of it.

The Tombs of Atuan starts with the tale of a young girl. She was born as the old Arha died, taken from her family once she survived to the age of five, and raised as the newest in a long line of reborn priestess of dark, mostly forgotten gods.

Long exposures at the country fair!

item.title: A Parade of Horribles
item.description:
Hazards: Well, we have the hail and the gatekeeper monster, whatever that might be. But I’d suggest that our biggest hazard is the fact that this bucket has to be driven by a cat this time.

And we’re back into the universe of Dungeon Crawler Carl!

On one side, we have floor ten and it’s full on Wacky Races style. We have crawlers (and now NPCs) given random cars (or giant living mounts)–Carl and Donut for example get a food truck (spoilers). And then they have to race. Just get to the finish line.

item.title: A week near Myrtle Beach
item.description:
A family trip to the beach–and a lot of birds. Also a few other fun pictures. But mostly birds.

item.title: The Mark of Athena
item.description:
“And,” Annabeth continued, “it reminds me how long we’ve known each other. We were twelve, Percy. Can you believe that?”
“No, he admitted. “So…you knew you liked me from that moment?”
She smirked. “I hated you at first. You annoyed me. Then I tolerated you for a few years. Then—”
“Okay, fine.”
…

The one about Athena/Annabeth.

We have the crew of the Argo II on their way to where it all began in Rome/Greece. And if that wasn’t enough, Annabeth has been given the titular Mark of Athena. And when anyone in universe hears about this, there are gasps and sideeyes, so you know that’s not going to be anything good.

item.title: Twelve Months
item.description:
What is this? New Dresden Files?! Count me in!

Twelve Months takes place in the year (heh) after Peace Talks and Battle Ground. And in a lot of ways, it’s a book about healing and moving on. Which, after the absolute mess that Battle Ground made of Chicago in general and Dresden in particular?

“A wizard is never late,” I muttered. “He arrives as soon as he’s dealt with his PTSD.”

item.title: Minions
item.description:
Scarlett Overkill: Work for me, and all this will be yours: respect, power…
Stuart the Minion: Banana!
Scarlett Overkill: …Banana!

The kids have been obsessed with Despicable Me recently, so of course we’d have to get back to the Minions.

On the surface, this is a movie that makes a lot of sense (take the cute little guys that were a breakout hit in Despicable Me and give them their own movie) and at the same time… no sense at all (for the same reason).

item.title: There Is No Antimemetics Division
item.description:
Welcome to the Antimemetics Division. No, this is not you first day.

So… basically SCP Foundation fanfic gone solo?

Which makes it sound so much worse than it is. It’s really an absolutely bundle of fascinating ideas, a nice heap of existential dread, and an at times rough/how in the world are we getting out of this one plot.

I enjoyed it.

In a nutshell, we have a mysterious secret society that is dealing with the supernatural and just plain unexplainable parts of the world.

item.title: Strange Practice
item.description:
Whatever you’re into is some fascinatingly weird shit.

It’s always interesting what jobs the point of view of an urban fantasy book has. In the Dresden Files, we start out with a Private Investigator. In the Mercy Thompson books, a mechanic. In Rivers of London, a cop.

In Strange Practice, we have a doctor (of the supernatural).

“You are not humans," she said at last, “but you are people . All of you. The ghouls, the mummies, the sanguivores, the weres, the banshees, the wights, the bogeys, everyone who comes to me for help, everyone who trusts me to provide it. You are all people , and you deserve to to be able to seek and receive that care without putting yourselves in jeopardy. What I do is necessary, and while it isn’t in the slightest bit easy, it is also the thing I want to do more than anything else in the world.”

item.title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
item.description:
How many Fantastic Four movies is that, just since 200? Four?

I think I’ve actually seen them all. One even had a sequel And I’m not sure I can remember anything from any of them really.

This one has a nice cast, a fun, well done retro-futuristic aesthetic, found family, and some future/world building potential. It’s not the best MCU movie by any standard, but I think it might just be the best Fantastic Four film.

item.title: Thunderbolts*
item.description:
Yelena Belova: There’s something wrong with me. An emptiness. I thought it started when my sister died, but now it feels like something bigger. Just a void. Or maybe I’m just bored.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe has been a little rough for a while. A few good movies, but mostly, everything mostly feels by the book.

Thunderbolts*… is a surprisingly good movie.

It could have been forgettable. More action movie/big skybeam showdown/forgettable mirror villains. It could have been Marvel’s answer to The Suicide Squad (either really).

item.title: The Son of Neptune
item.description:
The Lost Hero followed newcomer Jason Grace as he shows up at Camp Half-Blood, lacking in memories and with a touch of … Rome about him.

So of course, now in The Sons of Neptune we get the other side of the story.

Percy Jackson, also with memories missing, finds his way to Camp Jupiter instead. What if Camp Half-Blood, but Roman. And based on legion, with a much more militaristic point of view. It’s a really fascinating bit of world building–which we only had hints of in The Lost Hero–but I really do love how it expands this universe. Seeing different aspects of the gods we’ve been introduced too–and finding the ones that have no Greek counterparts.

item.title: Long Black (and White) Train (Tracks)
item.description:
Yeah, I know. Something of a tortured title.

It’s fun looking at train tracks though. I had no idea that they were as irregular as they are. Variations in spacing and alignment all over the place.

View on Flickr

item.title: Mad Men: Season 2
item.description:
I think that’s probably about enough Mad Men.

I’m still not entirely sure what people see in this show. Perhaps it’s coming from my (strong) preference for sci-fi and fantasy–worlds that really make me stretch, things that aren’t quite so real. Perhaps it’s the fact that no one in the show is really a particularly good person.

On a more positive note, I feel like more happened this season. And some of it was kind of crazy. Relationship drama in the Draper household (for good reason). Relationship drama with just about everyone else. Don just… taking off in California, with flashbacks filling in more of that backstory. Corporate drama shaking up the office politics.

item.title: Hadestown: The Musical
item.description:
♬ ♬ ♬
Way down Hadestown
Way down under the ground
♬ ♬ ♬

Hadestown is such a great show.

I first discovered the music a few years ago and listened to it almost non-stop. Then last year, I had a last minute chance to travel to New York and happened into last minute (excellent) tickets to see it on Broadway. Barely any of the original cast1, but it’s still an awesome show.

item.title: A Wizard of Earthsea
item.description:
You thought, as a boy, that a mage is one who can do anything. So I thought, once. So did we all. And the truth is that as a man’s real power grows and his knowledge widens, ever the way he can follow grows narrower: until at last he chooses nothing, but does only and wholly what he must do…

A Wizard of Earthsea is a relatively simple coming of age story about Ged. He starts out as a young boy, full of ideas and power, making a name for himself young. Then he takes one step too far, summons a dark being from outside of the world… and then he spends the rest of the book dealing with that.

item.title: Ocean's Twelve
item.description:
Ocean’s Eleven was great. A straight forward heist (at least in what their goal was) with enough twists about how they got it done that really drug you through the movie. All held up by an excellent (and stacked) cast and a ton of banter.

Ocean’s Twelve has pretty much the same cast, which I loved. But the heist makes so much less sense this time around. They do try to justify it (Benedict wants his money back), but it just feels a lot more disjoint. And the final twist, much less earned.

item.title: Frozen II
item.description:
Well, it’s not quite Frozen, but you know? I’m glad they really went for something ambitious!

It’s the same world. One kingdom (really one city on the coast). Sisters, one with powers and a queenship and the other with … an impressively positive attitude? Also, reindeer, a living snowmen, and now… elemental powers, mystical fog shrouded woods, and a voice calling out from … somewhere?

Olaf: I bet you’re wondering who we are and why we’re here. It’s really quite simple. It began with two sisters. One born with magical powers, and one born powerless, with her love of snowmen, infinite.

item.title: Matilda
item.description:
Matilda: Daddy, you’re a crook.
Harry Wormwood: What?
Matilda: This is illegal.
Harry Wormwood: [hands the car drill to Mikey, then walks to Matilda] You make money? Do you have a job?
Matilda: No, but don’t people need good cars? Can’t you sell good cars, Dad?
Harry Wormwood: Listen, you little wiseacre: I’m smart, you’re dumb; I’m big, you’re little; I’m right, you’re wrong, and there’s nothing you can do about it.

item.title: Alaska
item.description:
Twenty years later, another trip to Alaska. We met my parents (who were on a two month trip of their own) for one week. And oh, what a place for taking pictures Alaska is.

item.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
item.description:
Another long flight back? The perfect time to rewatch the Lord of the Rings.

Or perhaps just one of them–with the Extended Edition. Man those are long movies (especially in that version).

And man, I forgot just how awe inspiring those movies are.

It all began with the forging of the Great Rings.

It’s the tale of a little man (literally in this case) on a mission oh so very much larger than him–and even larger still; than perhaps he realizes.

item.description:
Our last full day. A bit quieter. We went to a museum and a store with a chocolate fountain.

Such a great trip. I’m ready to head home.

item.title: The Lost Hero
item.description:
Another day, another hero.

This time around, we open with Jason. Another obvious (to the reader) demigod, hidden in plain sight. Battle reflexes, special powers, purple T-shift… ability to speak Latin…

Jason scratched his head. “You named him Festus? You know that in Latin, ‘festus’ means ‘happy’? You want us to ride off to save the world on Happy the Dragon?

Wait. What?

Oh we’re in for a ride this time.

Our first day in Alaska, at a house just outside of Seward. Man. The forests and mountains and rivers and life just everywhere. It’s very pretty.

item.title: Ocean's Eleven
item.description:
It’s been a while since I watched these movies. But hey, when you’re on a plane for five hours and they have a screen full of movies? Worth!

In a nutshell–it’s a quintessential heist movie. Gather the crew, plan the heist, deal with what goes wrong, and walk away in the end victorious. And then show the audience how in the world you actually pulled it off.

Building the crew? Great.

item.title: The Karate Kid
item.description:
Miyagi: Wax on, wax off. Wax on, wax off.

Oh this movie. It’s a classic, but somehow I’ve never actually seen it. Right now is the second best time though, so here we go!

In a nutshell, it’s a pretty straight forward coming-of-age / underdog sports movie from the 80s. Really. Daniel moves to a new town, gets beat up, meets the girl, gets beat up some more, meets the mysterious mentor figure, learns (but doesn’t realize it), learns (but does), loses the girl, gets her back, and, in the end, wins the day.

item.title: Austin Powers in Goldmember
item.description:
It took a while (relatively speaking) to get to this one. And, while this one has a lot of great individual scenes, I think it’s the weakest of the series.

This time around, we’re in the 70s, with the introduction of Beyoncé’s Foxxy Cleopatra. I enjoyed her role, especially her introduction, talking (so obviously) through a third party. She seems like she’s having fun and is a good counterpoint to Austin.

item.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
item.description:
Onward in Harry Potter. And still without making it back to the first.

Plotwise, this is one of my favorites. It’s an action packed story with a lot of mystery going on and a twist to the plot that (long ago) I did not see coming–and which actually pulls the last part of the story together very well. Even if, in the broader world Harry Potter lives in doesn’t make any sense.

item.title: The Martian
item.description:
He’s stuck out there. He thinks he’s totally alone and that we all gave up on him. What kind of effect does that have on a man’s psychology?” He turned back to Venkat. “I wonder what he’s thinking right now.”

LOG ENTRY: SOL 61 How come Aquaman can control whales? They’re mammals! Makes no sense.

With the recent release of the Project Hail Mary movie, I decided to reread the Project Hail Mary book. So of course I also had to re-read The Martian (I’ll watch it at some point too!). But the last time I read it, I wasn’t writing reviews yet… so here we are!

item.title: The Last Olympian
item.description:
This is it! The Last Battle1. Kronos and his army of titans, monsters, gods, and demigods is about to reach New York City and Mount Olympus. And, because of a rampaging Titan coming across the country, the city is almost entirely undefended.

So it’s up to Percy and the demigods of Camp Half-Blood to save the day!

Oh, did I mention that Percy is about ot turn 16 in this book? And that there’s a certain prophecy all about that?

item.title: Despicable Me
item.description:
I watched (and reviewed) Despicable Me 2 years ago, in theaters. We watched those movies over and over again for so long when my children were younger. But now, it’s back in favor, so it’s a good time to review it!

Gru, criminal mastermind, has a glorious plan.

Gru: …we are going to steal… pause for effect… THE MOON!

To do that, he needs cookie robots and three little girls to deliver them. And oh, the girls are a delight. Margo, serious and holding everything together. Edith, agent of chaos. And Agnes. Just, cute.

item.description:
With my new lens, birds are so much easier to take pictures of. And they’re so dynamic. And sometimes weird looking.

item.title: The Demigod Files
item.description:
I probably should have skipped this one.

I do like the three short stories well enough.

We get The Bronze Dragon–a game of capture the flag and a new guardian for the camp. Plus we get more of Silena (child of Aphrodite) and Beckendorf (Hephaestus) who are a fun couple.

Then the Sword of Hades–I do enjoy stories with Nico in them. He’s a nicely complicated character. Plus more Thalia! It’s also fun to see Hades and Persephone bickering.

item.title: The Princess Bride
item.description:
A rewatch for me, but that’s just a fun movie. More than a bit 80s feeling, but it works. I love the characters, especially Andrew the Giant’s Fezzik and Wallace Shawn’s Vizzini. They’re just fun throughout the movie.

And man is this movie quotable.

Even if you haven’t seen, it I’m sure you’ll have heard some of these.

Inigo Montoya: Hello. My name is Inigo Montoya. You killed my father. Prepare to die.

item.title: The Battle of the Labyrinth
item.description:
The Labyrinth. Daedalus. Return of the Minotaur. Oh, this book has a lot going for it.

I love the setting. It’s interesting seeing more of the ways demigods can go–and have gone in the past. Not all demigods are heroes–which we’ve already seen–but they’re not always villains either. And the same with monsters; we’ve already met Tyson. And for that matter, gods and titans.

There are still good guys and bad guys. But everything is starting to get just a bit more complicated, which I appreciate in the series.

item.title: The Titan's Curse
item.description:
Annabeth is missing and a goddess is in chains! It’s time for a quest!

Only this time, it’s not Percy’s quest.

Oh, and apparently not everyone is fated to survive.

Percy is growing up–ever nearer to that fated 16th birthday. So of course, he’s got more than just demigod problems.

“Love conquers all," Aphrodite promised. “Look at Helen and Paris. Did they let anything come between them?”

“Didn’t they start the Trojan War and get thousands of people killed?”

item.title: The Sea of Monsters
item.description:
Families are messy. Immortal families are eternally messy. Sometimes the best we can do is to remind each other that we’re related for better or for worse…and try to keep the maiming and killing to a minimum.

After the events of The Lightning Thief, Percy Jackson is starting to settle into his world of gods and monsters. So of course, things have to get complicated.

This time around, we get a new friend (Tyson, a 6'3" seventh grader who’s a bit slower and absolutely obsessed with Percy), a new quest (the borders of Camp Half-Blood are failing!), and a whole new adventure: The Sea of Monsters.

item.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
item.description:
The Harry Potter films have some problems1, but they came out just at the right time to be a large part of my growing up. I’ve seen them all and, while I think the books are better in a lot of ways, the movies have a lot of charm. Especially the first few.

They’re just done in such a magical way, really capturing the fantastic feel of the world. It makes you wish you could just hop right in and explore the world, Hogwarts castle especially.

item.title: El Principito
item.description:
El Principito. En español. ¿Por qué? ¡Por qué no!

En serio, porque estoy aprendiendo español. Un libro fácil es bueno para aprender.

Pero El Principito es un libro raro.

Es un libro sobre serpientes. Y planetas. Y flores.

Y volcanes.

Y baobabs.

Como dije. Un libro raro.

Pero lo disfruté. [[TODO:El Ojo del Mundo||La próxima vez]], debería leer un libro en inglés y luego en español.

Voy!

item.title: Austin Powers: The Spy Who Shagged Me
item.description:
Where Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery was a delightful, raunchy, vulgar parody of spy flicks and the 90s, The Spy Who Shagged Me turns everything up a notch–for better and for worse.

It all starts out where the previous movie ended. Austin and Vanessa married and on their honeymoon. Except, surprise! Fembot. Which makes absolutely no sense. But I do appreciate that we get Heather Graham’s Felicity Shagwell out of it!

item.title: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery
item.description:
Austin Powers: Allow myself to introduce… myself.

Austin Powers. A riff on 60’s culture and especially the genre of spy movies (James Bond especially) absolutely loaded with a particularly rauncy, vulgar sort of humor.

Vanessa Kensington: Mr. Powers, my job is to acclimatize you to the nineties. You know, a lot’s changed since 1967.
Austin Powers: No doubt, love, but as long as people are still having promiscuous sex with many anonymous partners without protection while at the same time experimenting with mind-expanding drugs in a consequence-free environment, I’ll be sound as a pound!
